MLOps - Build a local KB with Ollama and Open WebUI

Jan 19, 2025

Continue Local MLOPS Project

In this post, I want to build a local Knowledge Base using WSL, Docker, Ollama and Open WebUI.

Ollama is a desktop application designed to run and interact with large language models (LLMs) locally on a machine. It provides an easy interface for downloading, managing, and using various LLMs, ensuring privacy and local execution.

Open WebUI is a web-based user interface for interacting with AI models. It is often used in conjunction with locally hosted or remote LLMs, providing a customizable and user-friendly platform to input queries and manage model interactions.

Here is what I am going to build:

  • A local RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) system

  • Using Ollama as the LLM server

  • Open WebUI as the frontend interface

  • Running everything through Docker/WSL

  • Build Knowledge base from some aged tech docs and Zack blogs

  • Query KB from the web interface with prompt

Get Started

Since I already have WSL, Nvidia Drviers, CUDA, Python, Docker Desktop ready by following the previous MLOPS posts, In order to have the docker container can access GPU, I still need nvidia-container-toolkit to be installed

Install Ollama and Open WebUI

  • Follow Ollama website, run bellow script to install Ollama server.
  • Follow Open WebUI Github, install Open WebUI using docker, by confituring ollama API URL and docker persistent volume, Open WebUI will show the models running within Ollama, all the configuration and dialogue history data also can be persist after server and application restart.
  • Open web browser and navigate to http://localhost:3000/ to access Open WebUI. First time access, you will be prompted to create a new admin account.

  • Start a dialogue to compare 3 modles qwen:7b, llama3:8b and mistral, obviouly llama3:8b is better then the other 2 models.

Build knowledge base collections

Building knowledge base collections in Open WebUI typically involves organizing, indexing, and embedding relevant data so that it can be queried effectively by the LLM.

  • Prepare Source Data

I have some aged Linux, VMware and Windows admin docs in my computer with Microsoft word format, I will use them to build some testing knowledge base collections, then I will upload the recent Zack bolg posts withas Markdown format as well, so from the dialogue it can be easier indexing and retrieval.

  • Enable Retrieval Features and Test Knowledge Base Configure Open WebUI to use the knowledge base during interactions. This involve enabling a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) feature or linking the embeddings to the model.

Using # in the beginning of the prompt to enable RAG feature, choose the knowledge collection from the collections we built earlier.

Start a dialogue and choose llama3:8b model, use the knowledge base collections zacl blog 2024 as reference to provide answer to summarize the posts I created 2024:

Conclusion

Now I have successfully built a local Knowledge Base (KB) using Ollama and Open WebUI. Here’s a very brief summary:

  • What I Did:

Set up GPU-enabled Docker/WSL environment.

Installed Ollama to run LLMs locally as a server.

Installed Open WebUI for a web-based interface to interact with LLMs.

Configured the system to enable Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with Docker volumes for persistence.

  • What YoIu Achieved:

Created a local RAG system capable of querying knowledge from aged tech docs and Zack blog posts.

Demonstrated effective model comparisons and knowledge-based querying through a user-friendly web interface.
